piece_type: Instagram post (reel + caption) on company and brand accounts
claim_text: “I’m excited about getting rid of my lines…I’m ready to, like, not have them so much.” | “I feel really good. I’m really surprised at how quickly it’s kicking in! And I’m feeling like the line between my eyebrows is gone.” | “*About 50% of patients begin showing improvement after two days. Most patients (~69%) achieve complete results by day 30.”
context: Patient testimonial reel with Day 0/Day 2/Day 30 before-and-after clips; full indication shown only at close of testimonial or by scrolling caption; SUPER 'Individual results may vary' does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Indication is temporary improvement in glabellar lines; GLS score of 0 ('none') was exploratory with no alpha, so claims that lines are 'gone' or results 'complete' are unsupported.
suggested_check: Does the piece imply complete/permanent elimination of the condition when the label supports only temporary or partial improvement?

piece_type: Instagram post (reel + caption) on company and brand accounts
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
claim_text: “Lines today. Blurred in as little as 2 days.*…Nope. You’re not seeing things. Jeuveau® really does work like that.” | “With our iconic fast-acting results…”
context: Day 2 data were an exploratory endpoint (>=1-point GLS change, single assessor) intermingled with primary Day 30 composite >=2-point endpoint. OPDP advisory comments (Nov 22, 2019) previously warned about onset claims.
fda_rationale: Onset claims rest on exploratory Day 2 endpoint without multiplicity adjustment and a less stringent response definition; mixing it with the primary endpoint misleads on onset and magnitude.
suggested_check: Are speed-of-onset claims ('fast-acting', 'as little as X days') based on a primary/prespecified endpoint, and are differing endpoint definitions kept distinct?

piece_type: Instagram post (reel + caption) on company and brand accounts
claim_text: “…it’s no wonder Jeuveau is making moves to Studio @IPSY for our Blur The Lines Masterclass. Because in 2026, we’re blurring the lines between what’s found in your beauty bag and what happens in the treatment room. [syringe icon] [lipstick icon]”
context: Lively testimonial with upbeat music, fashion/beauty styling; product carries boxed warning for distant spread of toxin effect.
fda_rationale: Likens a prescription injectable with a boxed warning to an everyday cosmetic, oversimplifying dosing/administration requirements and minimizing risk.
suggested_check: Does the piece equate a prescription drug with a cosmetic/consumer product or routine in a way that trivializes administration requirements or risks?

piece_type: Instagram post (reel + caption) on company and brand accounts
category: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
letter_category_label: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
claim_text: Risk information presented only at the end of the reel, after the tag line “Jeuveau, you see me” appears for about four seconds against a black background; unnarrated, fast scrolling risk information follows a directive to “ask your doctor if Jeuveau is right for you.”
context: No signal alerts viewers that risk info follows the 38-second testimonial; caption risk info only reachable by scrolling past additional benefit claims.
fda_rationale: Risk information lacks prominence and readability reasonably comparable to benefit presentation, minimizing risks.
suggested_check: Rule: in video/social pieces, flag if risk information appears only after a closing tag/end card, is unnarrated or fast-scrolling, or requires scrolling past benefit claims.

claim_text: “A STRONGER FOUNDATION FOR KIDNEY PRESERVATION” (page 1) | “Consistent nephroprotection” (pages 1 and 3) | “Achieving complete remission of proteinuria (defined as <0.3 g/d) drives long term nephroprotective benefits” (page 2) | “Kidney Function Preservation” (page 3) | “Proven to achieve better kidney function preservation over 2 years” (page 8) | “FILSPARI®: a stronger foundation for kidney preservation” (page 13)
context: PI indication: 'to slow kidney function decline'; eGFR slope -3.0 vs -4.2 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr vs irbesartan.
fda_rationale: Drug slowed the rate of decline but kidney function still declined, so 'preservation'/'nephroprotection' claims overstate the demonstrated effect.
suggested_check: Does the claim describe the outcome more strongly than the labeled effect (e.g., 'preserves/protects' when label says 'slows decline')?

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
claim_text: a bar graph with the heading “Proven to drive 3x more patients to complete remission of proteinuria (<0.3 g/day)” (page 7) | “Proven to drive 3x more patients to complete remission of proteinuria” (page 13)
context: Footnote disclaimer 'Prespecified exploratory analysis...' acknowledged but does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Complete remission was an exploratory endpoint with no alpha allocated; 'proven' claims are unsupported.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'proven'/'demonstrated' language attached to any endpoint labeled exploratory, post hoc, or not alpha-controlled in the same piece.

claim_text: “FILSPARI was well tolerated over 2 years” | “No drug-induced liver injury following treatment with Filspari” in conjunction with an image of a liver
context: Boxed Warnings for hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; REMS with liver monitoring; DILI cases occurred.
fda_rationale: Tolerability and 'no DILI' claims minimize serious boxed-warning risks; risk info elsewhere does not mitigate.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'well tolerated' and 'No [boxed-warning risk]' claims when the product label has a boxed warning or REMS for that risk.

claim_text: a graph depicting mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure over 110 weeks with the headline, “Blood pressure remained consistent over a 2-year period and was comparable to irbesartan”
context: PI W&P: greater incidence of hypotension-associated adverse events vs irbesartan; hypotension info on pages 10 and 15 does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Implies drug will not adversely affect blood pressure despite labeled hypotension risk.
suggested_check: Does a safety/tolerability graphic or headline imply absence of a risk that appears in the label's Warnings and Precautions?

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: “HELP PREVENT RSV DISEASE IN INFANTS WITH BEYFORTUS® AND SEE HOW YOU CAN AFFECT POPULATION HEALTH” | “Beyfortus is a monoclonal antibody that helps prevent RSV disease starting from Day 1 after injection.” | “Your efforts in immunizing infants against RSV disease can impact the population health burden in your community.”
context: Full indication ('prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease') and 'RSV-LRTI' appear further down, insufficient to correct the impression.
fda_rationale: Claims suggest general prevention of RSV disease (upper and lower) while indication is limited to lower respiratory tract disease.
suggested_check: Rule: compare indication phrases in headlines/body to the label indication string; flag when qualifiers (e.g., 'lower respiratory tract') are dropped.

claim_text: VO: “The one thing I love about the TOBI Podhaler is when I am running late, I can do it on the way to school in the car.” | VO: “My favorite things about the TOBI Podhaler are how portable it is, how quick it is to use, and how you can use it anywhere.” | VO: “We have used it on vacation, in the car, and while running out of the door on the way to school.”
context: IFU requires hand washing, clean dry surface, adequate lighting to inspect capsules, moisture protection, and 4-capsule repeat steps; some use info in the video does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Implies administration can be done anywhere without concern, contrary to IFU steps; improper handling may cause suboptimal dosing.
suggested_check: Do convenience claims ('anywhere', 'on the go', 'quick') conflict with Instructions for Use requirements for administration, handling, or storage?

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Omission of material facts about indication
claim_text: Beginnings of the videos introduce the use of Photofrin for the treatment of esophageal cancer (EC) and high-grade dysplasia in Barrett’s esophagus (EC video) and endobronchial non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC video), but omit specific patient populations and limitations.
context: Full indications appear only at end, small plain font, ~5 seconds, alongside risk info.
fda_rationale: Failing to disclose full indications (populations and limitations) misleads about approved use.
suggested_check: Rule: the first mention of each indication must include the label's population and limitation qualifiers; flag abbreviated indication statements.

claim_text: Videos do not communicate contraindications (“PHOTOFRIN is contraindicated in patients with porphyria …”; “PDT is contraindicated in patients with tumors eroding into a major blood vessel.”) or W&P 5.1 fistula/perforation, 5.2 hemorrhage, 5.4 photosensitivity (all patients), 5.8 airway obstruction, 5.12 embryo-fetal toxicity.
context: Some risk info at ~0:56 for about 10 seconds; rest only in final 5 seconds.
fda_rationale: Omitting serious contraindications and warnings creates a misleading impression of safety.
suggested_check: Rule: check that every contraindication and boxed/W&P item in the label appears in the piece's risk presentation.

claim_text: VO (2:32) (in pertinent part): “… selectively destroys the cancer cells with … a diameter of up to 1.2cm”
context: PI: PDT not suitable for patients with esophageal ulcers >1 cm in diameter.
fda_rationale: Suggests patients with ulcers >1 cm can be safely treated, contradicting contraindication.
suggested_check: Do any numeric eligibility/size claims conflict with contraindication thresholds in the label?

category: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
letter_category_label: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
claim_text: “IMPORTANT WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS” presented as static, onscreen text, in small, plain font, over approximately five seconds at the end of the video, in conjunction with the indications and most common adverse reactions.
context: Benefit claims in large print with colorful animated graphics; no signal that risk info follows the close of the animated portion.
fda_rationale: Risk not presented with prominence and readability reasonably comparable to benefits.
suggested_check: Rule: flag video pieces where risk text is on screen for less time / smaller font than benefit text or appears only after the end of the main content.

claim_text: “Following photodynamic therapy. Debridement may be performed if residual tumor remains” (3:34 – 3:36)
context: PI describes 'mandatory debridement bronchoscopy' 2 to 3 days after light administration for endobronchial cancer.
fda_rationale: Suggests debridement is optional when label says it is mandatory.
suggested_check: Does the piece describe a label-mandated procedure or monitoring step as optional?

claim_text: VO (3:07): “Photodynamic therapy is proven to boost anti-tumor immunity and improves tumor cell immunogenicity, essentially training the body to attack the invading cancer.” | SUPER (3:14): “Systemic Neutrophilia, Acute Phase Reactants, Inflammatory Cytokines, T- Cells*”
context: Supported only by a review article describing PDT generally in animal models, not Photofrin specifically.
fda_rationale: 'Proven' immune-boosting claim lacks support for Photofrin.
suggested_check: Is each 'proven' mechanism claim supported by evidence specific to this product in humans rather than class-level or animal data?

claim_text: VO (2:31): “The energy transfer generates reactive singlet oxygen which selectively destroys the cancer cells with … a diameter of up to 1.2cm.”
context: No references cited.
fda_rationale: Implies definitive, quantified NSCLC benefit not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Rule: flag quantitative efficacy claims with no reference citation attached.

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: “Try Sucraid®” | “Do you have patients suffering with unresolved IBS-like symptoms, including gas, bloating, diarrhea, and/or nausea?” | “Could it be CSID?” | “Learn more about the only FDA-approved enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of CSID...”
context: Full indication ('treatment of sucrase deficiency, which is part of CSID') only at bottom with ISI in small plain font after eye-catching graphics.
fda_rationale: Implies use for IBS and for all contributing factors of CSID; indication is limited to sucrase deficiency.
suggested_check: Does the piece invite use in a broader population (e.g., symptom-based, related conditions) than the labeled indication?

claim_text: Emails omit WARNINGS: Severe Hypersensitivity Reactions; PRECAUTIONS: Increased Blood Glucose Concentration in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus; Dietary Starch Restriction (“Sucraid does not replace isomaltase...”).
fda_rationale: Omits material risk information from the PI.
suggested_check: Rule: verify each Warning and Precaution heading from the PI is represented in the piece's safety information.

letter_category_label: Minimization of risk (order of risk presentation)
claim_text: Risk information pertaining to the ADVERSE REACTIONS section of the PI is presented prior to the risk information pertaining to the PRECAUTION section of the PI (i.e., Increased Blood Glucose Concentrations in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus).
fda_rationale: Risk not disclosed in order of severity, framing serious risks as less serious.
suggested_check: Rule: risk statements must follow label severity order (Boxed Warning > Contraindications > W&P > Adverse Reactions).

claim_text: “There’s a lot to consider when finding the best CLL [chronic lymphocytic leukemia] treatment for you. Brukinsa brings clarity to your path ahead.” | “See your future clearly again” | SUPER “. . . CLEARLY BRUKINSA.”
context: Worried woman crosses a bridge then smiles on a mountaintop; PRO data from open-label SEQUOIA/ALPINE not prespecified or multiplicity-controlled.
fda_rationale: Implies improved emotional/physical functioning (HRQoL) not demonstrated; PRO data descriptive only.
suggested_check: Does the narrative/visual arc imply quality-of-life or emotional-functioning benefits not supported by controlled PRO data?

claim_text: “the only BTKi [Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitor] proven superior to both another BTKi and to chemotherapy” | “And Brukinsa had low rates of cardiovascular events including afib [atrial fibrillation]” | SUPER “Cardiovascular side effects ~2 years: 10% BRUKINSA vs 6% BR [bendamustine + rituximab] (grade 1-2); 21% BRUKINSA vs 30% ibrutinib (overall). Rate of atrial fibrillation (all grades): 3% BRUKINSA and BR (~2 years) 7% BRUKINSA vs 17% ibrutinib (42.5 months).” | patients “might do better with Brukinsa.”
context: Onscreen concerns like 'Cardiac complications concern me'; ALPINE not powered to show clinically meaningful AF difference.
fda_rationale: Implies superior cardiovascular safety vs ibrutinib and 'best' treatment, not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Are comparative safety claims vs a named competitor based on an adequately powered, prespecified comparison?

category: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
letter_category_label: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
claim_text: The major statement includes presentations where the verbatim complete transcript or verbatim key terms or phrases from the corresponding audio do not appear in dual modality, along with presentations where there is information in the SUPERs that is not from the corresponding audio.
fda_rationale: Fails to present the major statement concurrently in audio and text (dual modality).
suggested_check: Rule: compare TV ad audio transcript of the major statement with on-screen SUPER text; flag mismatches or missing key terms.

claim_text: Major statement is presented when the TV ad’s emotional story arc reaches its peak: the woman confidently crosses the bridge, high-fives her friend, browses a gift shop, and poses for a picture on the mountaintop.
fda_rationale: Compelling, attention-grabbing visuals interfere with comprehension of the major statement.
suggested_check: During the major statement, are visuals neutral, or do they show emotional peaks/scene changes that compete for attention?

piece_type: DTC YouTube video and Spanish-language TV ad
claim_text: AVO (0:29): “Nubeqa may cause serious side effects including heart disease and seizure.”
context: PPI: heart disease (ischemic heart disease) 'that can lead to death'; seizure: 'avoid activities where a sudden loss of consciousness could cause serious harm'.
fda_rationale: Names risks but omits material information on their seriousness (fatal outcomes) and precautions, misleading on safety.
suggested_check: When a risk is named in a DTC piece, does it convey the label's severity (e.g., fatal outcomes) and key precautions rather than just the risk name?

piece_type: DTC YouTube video and Spanish-language TV ad
category: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
letter_category_label: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
claim_text: The major statements include presentations where the verbatim complete transcript or verbatim key terms or phrases from the corresponding audio do not appear in dual modality.
fda_rationale: Major statement not presented concurrently in audio and text.
suggested_check: Rule: compare major-statement audio transcript with on-screen text for verbatim key terms.

piece_type: DTC YouTube video and Spanish-language TV ad
claim_text: Attention-grabbing visuals (e.g., vibrant colors, constant motion within the scenes, frame transitions and camera movements) and frequent scene changes during the presentation of the major statement.
fda_rationale: Visuals interfere with comprehension of the major statement.
suggested_check: Are there frequent scene changes, motion, or vibrant visuals during the major statement?

piece_type: DTC branded website (landing page and 'Responses' webpage)
claim_text: “Most people achieved a response with Niktimvo” | “75% of people (59 out of 79) experienced a response”
context: PI: no complete responses; all 59 responders were partial responses; CR/PR definitions shown but do not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Implies complete responses when 0% CR was observed.
suggested_check: Do response-rate claims disclose response type (e.g., all partial) when unqualified 'response' could imply complete response?

piece_type: DTC branded website (landing page and 'Responses' webpage)
claim_text: “Niktimvo may offer fast and lasting responses” | “In a study of people experiencing chronic GVHD symptoms after taking at least 2 therapies, Niktimvo™ (axatilimab-csfr) delivered fast and lasting responses” | “Niktimvo provided lasting responses o More than half (60%) of the people who showed a response to Niktimvo continued to respond for at least 1 year” (next to a flipping calendar image)
context: PI: median time to response 1.5 months (range 0.9-5.1); median duration of response 1.9 months; 60% measure excludes progression.
fda_rationale: 'Fast' and 'lasting' overstate onset and durability; alternative durability metric conflates measures.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'fast'/'rapid'/'lasting'/'durable' descriptors and require them to be checked against label median time-to-response and duration-of-response.

piece_type: DTC branded website (landing page and 'Responses' webpage)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (organ-level responses)
claim_text: “People achieved responses in multiple affected organs” | “Niktimvo may provide fast and lasting responses across a range of affected organs” with a body diagram of organ-specific response rates
context: Efficacy based on ORR across all organs, not individual organs.
fda_rationale: Organ-level response rates inflate perceived benefit and ignore progression in other organs.
suggested_check: Does the piece present subcomponent/organ-level results that were not the basis of approval as standalone efficacy?

piece_type: DTC branded website (landing page and 'Responses' webpage)
claim_text: “Niktimvo offered symptom improvement” | “44 out of 79 people who received Niktimvo (56%) reported improvement in the specific chronic GVHD symptoms assessed in the study.” | “Symptom improvement was defined as a reduction in chronic GVHD symptoms compared to the start of the study.”
context: PI: exploratory analysis of modified Lee Symptom Scale (symptom bother), not number of symptoms.
fda_rationale: Mischaracterizes an exploratory symptom-bother measure as reduction in symptoms.
suggested_check: Does the description of a PRO endpoint match what the instrument actually measures, and is its exploratory status respected?

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: “Recently diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma?” (Video ad 1) | “ADCETRIS plus CHP is an FDA-approved option for adults with certain CD30expressing T-cell lymphomas” (Video ad 1) | “ADCETRIS plus CHP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone) is approved for adults with certain previously untreated CD30-expressing peripheral T-cell lymphomas.” (Video ads 1-3) | “Making a treatment decision for T-cell lymphoma?” (Video ad 2) | “A new T-cell lymphoma diagnosis brings many questions.” (Video ad 3)
context: Full indication (sALCL or other CD30-expressing PTCL incl. AITL and PTCL-NOS) only at bottom after ISI.
fda_rationale: 'Certain' and general T-cell lymphoma language fails to specify subtypes, suggesting broader use.
suggested_check: Rule: flag vague qualifiers like 'certain' or disease-category terms in place of the label's specific subtype list in indication statements.

claim_text: Ads do not communicate CONTRAINDICATIONS: “ADCETRIS is contraindicated with concomitant bleomycin due to pulmonary toxicity…” or fatal outcomes from W&P: serious/opportunistic infections, SJS/TEN, hyperglycemia (“including fatal outcomes”).
fda_rationale: Omitting contraindication and fatal-outcome warnings minimizes risks.
suggested_check: Rule: check contraindications and any 'fatal' W&P language from the PI appear in the piece's risk content.

claim_text: “LUCEMYRA® IS THE ONLY FDA-APPROVED, NON OPIOID MEDICINE PROVEN TO HELP WITH SYMPTOMS OF OPIOID WITHDRAWAL.”
context: Other FDA-approved lofexidine products exist for the same indication.
fda_rationale: 'Only FDA-approved' exclusivity claim is false.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'the only' / 'first and only' / 'only FDA-approved' claims for mandatory verification against current approvals (incl. generics).

category: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
letter_category_label: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
claim_text: “Demonstrated safety profile in studies” | “Lofexidine should therefore be the preferred choice for withdrawal management in an outpatient setting, where monitoring of blood pressure and management of hypotension is more difficult”
context: Risk info only under collapsed header 'Click to see full Important Safety Information & Prescribing Information'; requires manual click to expand.
fda_rationale: Benefit claims prominent while risk info is hidden behind an expandable header, minimizing risk.
suggested_check: Rule: on webpages, flag when ISI/risk content is only in a collapsed/expandable element or behind a click while benefit claims are visible.

category: Failure to submit at first use (Form FDA 2253)
letter_category_label: Failure to submit at time of initial dissemination (Form FDA 2253)
claim_text: A copy of the webpage was not submitted to FDA under cover of Form FDA-2253 at the time of initial publication as required.
fda_rationale: Promotional materials must be submitted at first use with Form FDA-2253 and current labeling.
regulation: Form FDA-2253 submission requirement (21 CFR 314.81(b)(3)(i) per other OPDP letters; not numerically cited here)
suggested_check: Rule: before release, confirm a Form FDA 2253 submission record exists for the piece.

piece_type: DTC online video ('Ozempic vs. – Random Guy OLV')
category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: VO: (Stan): “Hm. Now it says here… for adults with type 2 diabetes, Ozempic is the GLP-1 with the most FDA-approved uses” | SUPER: “Ozempic® is the GLP-1 with the most FDA-approved uses for adults with type 2 diabetes.”
context: CV and CKD indications require concurrent established CV disease or CKD; full indications shown in SUPERs later do not correct VO.
fda_rationale: Implies all T2D patients are candidates for all indications.
suggested_check: Do claims aggregating multiple indications imply that the whole base population qualifies for each, ignoring required comorbidities?

piece_type: DTC online video ('Ozempic vs. – Random Guy OLV')
claim_text: “There’s Only One Ozempic. O, O, O.” | VO: (Stan): “Well, I see you don’t have as many FDA-approved uses as Ozempic.” | VO: (“other GLP-1s”): “Oh, really? Well, can Ozempic do this?” while making bird calling sound | 'Ozempic' character in bright orange shirt vs 'other GLP-1s' in dull gray shirt
context: Supporting trials were placebo-controlled, not designed to show superiority vs other GLP-1s.
fda_rationale: Comedic framing and visuals imply superiority over competitor GLP-1s without head-to-head data.
suggested_check: Do dialogue, humor, or visual contrasts (color, staging) imply superiority over a competitor class without head-to-head evidence?

piece_type: DTC online video ('Ozempic vs. – Random Guy OLV')
category: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
letter_category_label: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
claim_text: No signal alerts the viewer that important risk information follows the close of the interaction; the video shows the Ozempic logo and plays the musical “There’s Only One Ozempic . . . ”, which typically signals the close of an advertisement.
context: Statement directing to Ozempic-pi.com does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Placing risk after an apparent ending undermines risk communication.
suggested_check: Rule: flag video pieces where logo/jingle/end-card appears before the risk information.

company: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (letter addressed to Johnson & Johnson International, Inc.)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (responder subset / maintenance trial)
claim_text: “Many people experienced remission at 1 and even 2 years” (AVO) | “~1 out of 2 patients were in clinical remission at 1 year and at 2 years” (SUPER) | “MANY PEOPLE EXPERIENCED REMISSION at 1 and even 2 years” (SUPER)
context: UC2 maintenance enrolled only Week-12 responders (38-39% non-responders excluded); 2-year data from LTE subset of a subset.
fda_rationale: Applying maintenance/LTE responder rates to all treated patients overstates remission and durability.
suggested_check: Are rates from randomized-withdrawal/maintenance or extension responder subsets presented as if they apply to all treated patients?

company: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (letter addressed to Johnson & Johnson International, Inc.)
claim_text: “Some saw one hundred percent visible healing of their intestinal lining” (AVO, 0:18) | “Some saw 100% VISIBLE HEALING of their intestinal lining” (SUPER) | “Healing is possible with Tremfya” (AVO, 0:34) | “HEALING IS POSSIBLE with Tremfya® (guselkumab)” (SUPER)
context: Disclaimer 'Visually assessed areas may not represent remission of the entire colon lining. Individual results may vary.' does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Implies curative 'healing'; endoscopic endpoints don't guarantee long-term outcomes.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'heal/healing/cure/100%' language in chronic-disease efficacy claims.

company: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (letter addressed to Johnson & Johnson International, Inc.)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (responder subset / maintenance trial)
claim_text: “1 out of 3 patients achieved endoscopic remission at one year” (SUPER, 0:18 and 0:34)
context: 35%/34% at Week 44 in UC2 responder population.
fda_rationale: Suggests a third of all treated patients achieve endoscopic remission.
suggested_check: Is the denominator for a quoted rate (e.g., responders only) disclosed and consistent with the implied population?

company: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (letter addressed to Johnson & Johnson International, Inc.)
claim_text: The major statement does not communicate: “TREMFYA is a medicine that may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections.”
context: From Medication Guide 'most important information'.
fda_rationale: Omits material infection risk from major statement.
suggested_check: Rule: Medication Guide 'most important information' items must appear in a TV ad's major statement.

claim_text: “. . . turn the page with VONJO” (VO, 0:04-0:07) | “. . . ask your doctor if it’s time to turn the page with VONJO” (VO, 0:51-0:54)
context: Imagery of an elderly man walking his dog, eating ice cream, dancing; PERSIST-2 TSS coprimary endpoint failed vs best available therapy (p=0.08).
fda_rationale: Implies HRQoL/emotional/social functioning benefits not demonstrated; the symptom endpoint failed.
suggested_check: Do taglines and lifestyle imagery imply quality-of-life or symptom benefits that the trials did not demonstrate (or that failed)?

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: The TV ad suggests the use of Vonjo in adults with certain types of MF and “low” platelet counts, without specifying what is considered “low.”
context: PPI: platelet count below 50 x 10^9/L.
fda_rationale: Vague qualifier fails to communicate indicated population.
suggested_check: Rule: flag vague population qualifiers ('low', 'certain', 'some') where the label specifies a numeric threshold or subtype.

claim_text: Fails to communicate that bleeding can be severe, changes in electrical activity of the heart can be life-threatening, diarrhea is common and can also be severe, and increased risk of major cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death.
fda_rationale: Omits severity qualifiers and MACE risk from PPI.
suggested_check: Rule: compare each risk mention against PPI for severity words ('severe', 'life-threatening', 'death') and flag when dropped.

claim_text: Major statement presented during pop-up book theme: pages turn, background music changes, dog barking and scaring ducks, ice cream cart, dancing with dog by a busker.
fda_rationale: Attention-grabbing visuals, frequent scene changes, and music interfere with comprehension.
suggested_check: Are there scene changes, music changes, or engaging action during the major statement?

claim_text: “…and while I still have CIDP, I have a chance to live vividly.” | “Vyvgart Hytrulo has been proven to significantly reduce the risk of symptoms getting worse.” | “I’m hitting fairways with the fellas. I’m hitting the road with my number one. That’s how we live vividly with Vyvgart Hytrulo”
context: Patients with cane/leg braces shown golfing and driving; trial enrolled INCAT >=2 patients needing walking support; endpoint was time to clinical deterioration.
fda_rationale: Implies all patients can engage in such activities with little functional restriction; not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Do depicted activities imply a level of functional recovery beyond what the trial endpoint and enrolled population support?

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (hazard ratio as risk reduction)
claim_text: SUPER: “For patients identified as responders entering the main part of the study, the risk of arm and leg symptoms getting worse was 61% lower for patients taking VYVGART Hytrulo, compared to patients taking placebo (VYVGART Hytrulo=111 patients; placebo=110 patients).”

letter_category_label: Distracting presentation of material efficacy qualifier (SUPER)
claim_text: VO: “It’s a twice-daily pill that substantially improved hemoglobin levels compared to SOLIRIS® or ULTOMIRIS® infusions” | graphic: “IMPROVED HEMOGLOBIN LEVELS COMPARED TO SOLIRIS® OR ULTOMIRIS® INFUSIONS”

suggested_check: Rule: compute SUPER words-per-minute (words / on-screen seconds × 60); flag > ~238 wpm (FDA cites 175–300 range); flag when claim graphic is larger/more central than qualifying SUPER.

piece_type: HCP branded website webpages: “T315I Mutation”, “CML OPTIC Trial Efficacy”, “CML PACE Trial Efficacy” (USO-ICL-0558v4.0)

context: PI: MG-ADL change -3.4 vs -0.8 at day 43; separation at day 8 minimal and not significant.

piece_type: HCP branded website “SKYRIZI VS STELARA (ustekinumab)” webpage (US-SKZG-241257)
claim_text: “SKYRIZI vs STELARA® (ustekinumab)[;] SKYRIZI ACHIEVED SUPERIORITY ACROSS SEVERAL RANKED ENDPOINTS IN A HEAD-TO-HEAD STUDY” | “FIRST APPROVED CROHN’S DISEASE THERAPY THAT MET ENDOSCOPIC SUPERIORITY ENDPOINTS IN A HEAD-TO-HEAD TRIAL” | “~2X MORE PATIENTS ON SKYRIZI DEMONSTRATED ENDOSCOPIC REMISSION VS STELARA AT WEEK 48” | “SUPERIORITY MET ACROSS ENDOSCOPIC OUTCOMES” | “~2X MORE PATIENTS ON SKYRIZI WERE IN ENDOSCOPIC REMISSION WITHOUT STEROIDS (STEROID-FREE ENDOSCOPIC REMISSION) VS STELARA AT WEEK 48”
context: Phase 3b SEQUENCE open-label head-to-head; completion 90.2% vs 72.8%; missing week-48 endoscopy 16% vs 34%; unblinded endoscopist. Disclaimer: “DATA LIMITATION: The open-label nature of this study may have influenced these results”.
fda_rationale: Open-label design with differential dropout/missingness cannot support conclusory superiority; disclaimer does not cure.
suggested_check: Judge: head-to-head superiority claims — check blinding, differential dropout/missing data; open-label comparator studies need strong caution; disclaimer is not a fix.

piece_type: HCP website “Clinical Trial Results” webpage, “Additional Data” tab (TAZ-US-000086)

context: Tumor-volume-reduction percentages are effectively DCR (CR+PR+SD); approval on ORR/DOR in single-arm Study E7438-G000-101; LIMITATIONS disclaimers present; complaint received.

suggested_check: Rule: in single-arm-trial products, flag stable disease / DCR / waterfall plots including SD; disclaimers do not count as a fix. Also flag 'any reduction in tumor volume' percentages, which embed SD.

suggested_check: Judge: lifestyle/'carefree'/return-to-normal imagery in progressive disease where PI functional/QoL measures (e.g., 6MWT, KCCQ) still declined (slower decline ≠ improvement).

suggested_check: Rule: flag 'eliminate(s)', 'quickly', 'fast' combined with symptom/pain claims; require comparison to label responder rates and time point.

piece_type: DTC TV ad with celebrity spokesperson
claim_text: “One dose works fast to eliminate migraine pain”
context: 78-81% did not achieve pain freedom after one dose; label permits second dose after 2 hours.
fda_rationale: Implies all patients will be pain-free after a single dose.
suggested_check: Does a 'one dose' claim imply universal response when most patients did not respond or may need re-dosing?

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (single-arm; composite including stable disease)
claim_text: “DCR IN PATIENTS TAKING KRAZATI: 80% (n=112; 95% CI: 70.8-86.5)” | “Depth of response: 80% of patients experienced tumor shrinkage of any magnitude.” | “Stable Disease: 37%”
context: Waterfall plot; accelerated approval on ORR/DOR from single-arm KRYSTAL-1; Bad Ad complaints received.
fda_rationale: Stable disease in a single-arm trial cannot be attributed to the drug; DCR composite unsupported.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'disease control rate' or 'stable disease' claims sourced from single-arm studies.

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (single-arm time-to-event endpoints)
claim_text: “MEDIAN OS IN PATIENTS TAKING KRAZATI: 14.1 MONTHS” | “MEDIAN PFS IN PATIENTS TAKING KRAZATI: 6.9 MONTHS”
context: 'Descriptive analysis' label and disclaimer that single-arm trials don't characterize OS/PFS do not cure.
fda_rationale: Time-to-event endpoints in single-arm trials are uninterpretable.
suggested_check: Rule: flag OS/PFS/median survival claims whose source is a single-arm trial, regardless of disclaimers.

letter_category_label: Overstatement of efficacy (pooled data inconsistent with label)
claim_text: “DESCRIPTIVE ANALYSIS MEDIAN DOR IN PATIENTS TAKING KRAZATI: 12.5 MONTHS.”
context: PI median DOR 8.5 months (95% CI 6.2-13.8); claim based on pooled 'data on file'.
fda_rationale: Pooled data contradict and overstate labeled DOR.
suggested_check: Rule: numeric efficacy values must match the PI value for the same endpoint; flag discrepancies and 'data on file' / pooled sources.

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
claim_text: “33% INTRACRANIAL ORR IN PATIENTS WITH STABLE, ADEQUATELY TREATED BRAIN METASTASES” | “INTRACRANIAL DCR IN PATIENTS WITH BRAIN METASTASES: 85% (n=33; 95% CI: 68-95).”

suggested_check: Are subgroup results confounded by prior/concomitant therapy presented as drug effects?

piece_type: Instagram post by paid celebrity influencer (video + text)
claim_text: “So, I have an infant and a toddler both who have severe food allergies . . . . Auvi-Q is the only epinephrine autoinjector out there for infants and toddlers.” (AVO) | “AUVI-q® (epinephrine injection, USP) is for life-threatening allergic emergencies.” (SUPER) | “AUVI-q 0.1 mg is for infants and toddlers 16.5-33 lbs.” (text)
context: Post entirely omits risk information; 'For Important Safety Information, visit @auviq_ISI' does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Efficacy claims with no risk information create misleading impression of safety.
suggested_check: Rule: any piece with product name + benefit/use claim must contain risk information in the piece itself; a link/handle to ISI alone fails.

claim_text: VO: “And KISQALI helps preserve quality of life so you’re not just living, you’re living well.” | GRAPHIC: “PRESERVES QUALITY OF LIFE” | SUPER: “Quality of life was a secondary outcome measure of the trial. At a 26-month check-in, median time to worsening of at least 10% in quality of life score was 27.7 months with KISQALI + letrozole vs 27.6 months with placebo + letrozole. This analysis was not pre-planned to detect a false positive.”
context: MONALEESA-2 global QoL secondary endpoint with no alpha allocation; assessment intervals, 7-day recall, confounding, unvalidated 10% threshold, informative dropout.
fda_rationale: Exploratory PRO data cannot support 'preserves quality of life' or 'living well'; disclaimer insufficient.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'quality of life', 'living well', 'preserves QoL' claims and require an alpha-controlled PRO endpoint in the label.

letter_category_label: Distracting presentation of material efficacy qualifier (SUPER readability)
claim_text: “live longer” | “[l]ong live family time,” “[l]ong live dreams,” “long live you,” “[l]ong live hugs and kisses,” “long live life” | GRAPHIC “HELPS WOMEN LIVE LONGER” with SUPER: “Overall survival (OS) was a secondary end point of the trial... At an 80-month check in, median OS was 63.9 months for KISQALI + an NSAI [non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor] vs 51.4 months for an NSAI alone.”
context: SUPER presents 48 words in ~5 seconds (576 wpm vs ~238 wpm average) during competing audio, music, scene change, and larger graphics.
fda_rationale: Material information qualifying survival claims cannot be read or processed, creating misleading efficacy impression.
suggested_check: Rule: compute SUPER words-per-minute (words / seconds on screen x 60); flag > ~240 wpm, especially when competing graphics/audio are present.

product: PHEXXI (lactic acid, citric acid, and potassium bitartrate)
claim_text: “And in a separate analysis 99% of pregnancies were prevented per act of sex (101 pregnancies over 24,289 acts of sex).” | “Since Phexxi is an on-demand birth control, during the clinical trial, the effectiveness of Phexxi was also looked at each time Phexxi was used (per act of sex). This means Phexxi prevented pregnancy 99% of the time.”
context: PI: 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate 13.7% (86% prevention); Pearl Index 27.5 (72.5%); disclaimer 'These data are not found in the Product Information...' does not mitigate. Bad Ad complaint received.
fda_rationale: Per-act-of-sex metric is not validated and ignores fertile window; overstates efficacy vs labeled endpoints.
suggested_check: Rule: flag efficacy figures that differ from the PI's primary efficacy metric, and any claim with a 'not in the Prescribing Information' disclaimer.

piece_type: Consumer website webpages ('What is Recorlev?' and 'Taking Recorlev')
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “The SONICS clinical study supported the efficacy and safety results from LOGICS” o “31% of patients had normal cortisol levels after taking Recorlev for 6 months without changing their dose” o “67% of patients who moved on to the second part of the study had normal cortisol levels by the end of the study”
context: PI: 29/77 (38%) normal at end of maintenance; 16/77 (21%) at end of extended evaluation; 67% was end of titration; PI caveat that 51% discontinued prematurely omitted.
fda_rationale: 67% misstates the timepoint and overstates efficacy; omits material discontinuation caveat.
suggested_check: Rule: verify each quoted percentage matches the label value for the stated timepoint/phase; flag omission of label 'interpret with caution' caveats.

piece_type: Consumer website webpages ('What is Recorlev?' and 'Taking Recorlev')
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)

letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “Recorlev - More patients (52%) who were on a stable and steady dose of Recorlev had normal cortisol levels”
context: 52% = 11/21 randomized-withdrawal patients selected from 79 who had tolerated and responded.
fda_rationale: Enriched responder subset presented as general patient experience.
suggested_check: Are results from an enriched/randomized-withdrawal population presented as representative of all patients?

piece_type: Consumer website webpages ('What is Recorlev?' and 'Taking Recorlev')
claim_text: “As with other medicines for Cushing's, monitoring by your doctor is important so they know how you're doing” . . . “Heart and liver tests before and during treatment with Recorlev will help your doctor avoid side effects” | “Side effects can occur with Recorlev, including some that are serious”
context: Boxed warnings for hepatotoxicity and QT prolongation (13% DILI; 14.7% QTcF change >60 msec); boxed warnings relegated to middle of ISI without signal.
fda_rationale: Generic risk statement omits boxed warnings and implies monitoring lets patients 'avoid' side effects.
suggested_check: Rule: flag generic risk statements ('side effects can occur', 'some serious') and 'avoid side effects' language when the product has a boxed warning; boxed warning must lead the ISI.

claim_text: The post, titled “Slynd® (drospirenone),” presents claims and representations about the benefits of Slynd but fails to communicate any risk information.
context: Identified via OPDP surveillance.
fda_rationale: Complete omission of risk information.
suggested_check: Rule: any branded benefit claim requires risk information in the same piece.

letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “Offer your patients estrogen-free birth control with periods on a schedule.”
context: Scheduled bleeding fell from 81.2%/98.0% (Cycle 1) to 26.4%/28.4% (Cycle 13); 40.3%/52.2% unscheduled bleeding at Cycle 13.
fda_rationale: Most patients did not have scheduled periods over time.
suggested_check: Does a predictability/regularity claim reflect the long-term (not first-cycle) data in the label?

claim_text: Video prominently communicates that Trulicity can help “lower A1C along with diet and exercise,” but fails to adequately communicate the FDA-approved indication and limitations of use.
context: Indication/limitations only in small fast-scrolling font in a window at bottom, competing with fast visuals, scene changes, moving text and music. Bad Ad complaint; prior advisory comments.
fda_rationale: Implies Trulicity lowers A1C in all patients; omits limitations (not for T1D/DKA, pancreatitis, severe GI disease).
suggested_check: Rule: limitations of use from the label must appear with comparable prominence to the first benefit claim.

claim_text: Risk information in a small window relegated to the bottom of the post, presented using fast-paced, scrolling, small font, while benefit claims use colorful, fast-paced visuals, large-moving superimposed text and a strong, fast-moving musical beat.
fda_rationale: Risk not presented with comparable prominence and readability.
suggested_check: Rule: flag social video where risk appears only in a scrolling sub-window or small font relative to benefit text.

claim_text: Fails to include: “Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Your risk for getting low blood sugar may be higher if you use TRULICITY with another medicine that can cause low blood sugar, such as a sulfonylurea or insulin.”
fda_rationale: Omits material W&P information.
suggested_check: Rule: verify W&P conditional risks (e.g., with concomitant drugs) are stated, not just the risk name.

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ads (2; athlete sponsorship 'The Journey Forward')
letter_category_label: Omission of risk information (non-compliant reminder ad)
claim_text: “brought to you by Emgality proud partner of Team USA” with “I do a whole bunch of different things to try to prevent migraine because for me the pain is really tough” (Ryan Murphy TV Ad) | “By the time I was in college, migraine had me hiding from light and sound, it was isolating” (Allysa Seely TV Ad)
context: Ads reference indication so do not qualify as reminder ads under 21 CFR 202.1(e)(2); no risk information at all.
fda_rationale: Ads suggesting an indication must include major statement of side effects and contraindications.
suggested_check: Rule: if a piece names the product and mentions the disease/use, it is not a reminder ad and must include risk information.

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ads (2; athlete sponsorship 'The Journey Forward')
claim_text: The TV ads fail to either provide adequate provision or a brief summary as required by 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1).
fda_rationale: Broadcast ads require adequate provision for dissemination of labeling or a brief summary.
suggested_check: Rule: broadcast ads must include adequate provision elements (toll-free number, website, print ad reference, HCP referral) or a brief summary.

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ads (2; athlete sponsorship 'The Journey Forward')

claim_text: Ryan Murphy TV Ad suggests use for the preventive treatment of migraine but does not specify adults; Allysa Seely TV Ad suggests use for the treatment of migraine but does not specify preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
fda_rationale: Fails to communicate the full indication.
suggested_check: Rule: indication statements must include the label's population (e.g., 'adults') and use type (e.g., 'preventive').

fda_rationale: Required by 21 CFR 314.81(b)(3)(i).
suggested_check: Rule: confirm Form FDA 2253 submission at first use.

claim_text: “Hydrocortisone Oral Granules I Alkindi Sprinkle Now Available Accurate and individualized dosing for infants and children with adrenal insufficiency. Strengths as low as 0.5 mg without splitting or manipulation.” | “Hydrocortisone Oral Granules I Cortisol Replacement Therapy ALKINDI SPRINKLE: low-strength hydrocortisone for children with adrenal insufficiency. Individualized hydrocortisone dosing with no bitter taste, pill cutting or dissolving.” | “Alkindi Sprinkle for Kids I Micro-Granular Hydrocortisone Alkindi Sprinkle for pediatric adrenal insufficiency; strengths as low as 0.5 mg. No cutting, no splitting, just sprinkles for neonates and children <17 years of age.”
context: Google sponsored links; no risk information. Product W&P include adrenal crisis, infection, growth retardation, Cushing's syndrome, etc.
fda_rationale: Benefit claims with no risk information create a misleading impression of safety.
suggested_check: Rule: any short-form piece (search ad, banner) with benefit/indication claims must include risk information or be a compliant reminder piece.

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (real-world evidence / comparative)
claim_text: “In a Real-World Study with nearly 11,000 patients Pegfilgrastim PFS resulted in a significantly higher risk of FN vs. Onpro®” | “Across all cycles of chemotherapy, the incidence of FN associated with prefilled syringe (PFS) was 1.7% (n = 455) vs 1.3% (n = 126) for Neulasta® Onpro®” | “31%* *p = 0.01” | “With PFS, FN incidence increased by 31% vs Onpro®”
context: Retrospective claims study; unvalidated FN algorithm; no control for selection bias; absolute difference 0.4%; limitations in frames 7-8 do not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Study design limitations preclude comparative conclusions; reporting p-value is misleading; relative risk emphasized over small absolute difference.
suggested_check: Do comparative effectiveness claims rest on retrospective/RWE data with unvalidated outcome definitions or uncontrolled confounding? Is relative risk emphasized over absolute difference?

claim_text: “Pegfilgrastim PFS” presented as comparator vs “Neulasta Onpro” and “Onpro”
context: Use of nonproprietary name for PFS arm vs proprietary name for OBI; frame six statement that both arms were Neulasta was less prominent.
fda_rationale: Could lead HCPs to conclude biosimilar pegfilgrastim (PFS-only) is less effective than Neulasta Onpro.
suggested_check: Does naming of comparator arms (generic vs brand) imply inferiority of competitor/biosimilar products not studied?

piece_type: DTC sponsored TV talk-show segment video (celebrity spokesperson; ABC's The View, also YouTube)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “. . . something that works in about 15-30 minutes . . .” | “It literally works within, for me, 15 minutes. And anyone with a migraine, for 15 minutes, of pure agony, they’re like knives in my head. So to have this relief, and to not be in a fog afterwards . . . I’m able to just go with the rest of my day.”
context: Co-primary endpoints measured at 2 hours; no prespecified endpoints at 15 or 30 minutes; 'TREATMENT RESULTS MAY VARY' SUPER does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Spokesperson experience does not support onset claims not shown in trials.
suggested_check: Rule: flag onset-of-action time claims (minutes/hours) and verify against PI endpoint timepoints.

piece_type: DTC sponsored TV talk-show segment video (celebrity spokesperson; ABC's The View, also YouTube)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “I have been on handfuls of different prescriptions and over-the-counter medications, and none of them have really worked for me. Or if they worked, and maybe it was a one or two time thing and then they didn’t work consistently after that. And I was given Nurtec ODT, I tried it, it was a gamechanger[.]” | “So to have this relief, and to not be in a fog afterwards, to not like, other medications would give me rebound headaches, and this one doesn’t . . .”
fda_rationale: Implies superiority over other Rx/OTC products and significant advance ('gamechanger') not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Does a testimonial imply superiority or a breakthrough ('gamechanger') versus other treatments?

claim_text: “2.5mg/mL provides easy dose titration as body surface area-based dosing is recommended.”

claim_text: “I wanted to let you know that Xatmep® (methotrexate) oral solution is available for your patients with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.”

suggested_check: Rule: indication mentions must include population (pediatric) and regimen qualifiers (combination maintenance) from the PI.

claim_text: TV ad omits the contraindication for known hypersensitivity to glucagon or excipients and the W&P for hypersensitivity and allergic reactions; includes pheochromocytoma and insulinoma contraindications without the consequences (dramatic BP increase; hypoglycemia).
fda_rationale: Omitting serious risks and material facts suggests Gvoke is safer than demonstrated.

letter_category_label: Overstatement of efficacy (ease of use / administration)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “Easy to use. Easy to know you did it right. Pretty easy, huh?”
context: PI/IFU describe multiple preparation and administration steps; no signal to confirm correct administration; no supporting references.
fda_rationale: Ease-of-use and 'did it right' claims unsupported and oversimplify emergency administration.
suggested_check: Do ease-of-use claims oversimplify administration relative to the IFU, or claim user confirmation the device does not provide?

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Minimization of disease seriousness / omission of material facts
claim_text: VOICEOVER (VO): “If you have diabetes and take insulin, you know low blood sugar can be scary. You might start to sweat, panic, worry you might pass out. You may even feel like you’re falling.” | “I can be used even before passing out.”

fda_rationale: Presents mild symptoms only and omits when to administer and need for administration by others.
suggested_check: Does the piece depict the condition in a milder form than the indicated population, or omit who must administer and when?

claim_text: “. . . low blood pressure and fainting in certain settings . . . [,]” | [Omission] all contraindications; Boxed Warning details (alcohol close in time — wait at least 2 hours after 1–2 drinks; CYP3A4 inhibitors; liver problems); CNS depression W&P; hypotension/syncope with Addyi alone
context: Boxed Warning for hypotension and syncope. Prior OPDP advisory comments (2016) to Valeant.
fda_rationale: Omits contraindications and material Boxed Warning/W&P facts; misleading safety impression.
suggested_check: Rule: diff risk content vs Boxed Warning sub-elements, all contraindications and W&P headings.

category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts

claim_text: “1 in 10 premenopausal women suffer from frustrating low libido, also known as HSDD.” | “Meet Addyi – the first and only FDA-approved non-hormonal pill for acquired, generalized HSDD in premenopausal women. In other words: An FDA-approved pill for women frustrated by their low libido.” | “Ladies, add your desire back with Addyi.”

piece_type: DTC video “An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame, and the Weight Loss Revolution” (ABC primetime 3/18/2024; Hulu) featuring paid consultants and a Lilly executive
claim_text: [Omission] Boxed-warning contraindication for MEN 2 (only “anybody [who] has a history specifically of medullary thyroid cancer” discussed); W&Ps omitted: severe GI disease, acute kidney injury, hypersensitivity, hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications, suicidal behavior and ideation

piece_type: DTC video “An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame, and the Weight Loss Revolution” (ABC primetime 3/18/2024; Hulu) featuring paid consultants and a Lilly executive
claim_text: “There’s been a lot of hype around like pancreatitis, gallbladder complications, concerns for thyroid cancer. This has really not been shown in human studies that this is a downstream complication, and that really the risk is less than 1%.” | “If anybody has a history specifically of MTC... is very, very rare. ... recognizing that it’s rare, but it’s there and we have to always screen.”
context: W&P acute pancreatitis (incl. fatal hemorrhagic/necrotizing); gallbladder disease class W&P; class boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors; 15-yr MTC registry required.

piece_type: DTC video “An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame, and the Weight Loss Revolution” (ABC primetime 3/18/2024; Hulu) featuring paid consultants and a Lilly executive
claim_text: “I think that they’ve gotten overhyped. Medicines have side effects, but the important part is that they’re mild to moderate in the research studies.” | Dr. Butsch: “Yeah.”
context: Response to patient who discontinued due to nausea and vomiting blood. PI: GI ARs 56% vs 30% placebo (Zepbound); GI-related discontinuations up to 4.3%/6.6%; 'sometimes severe'.
